title: London Eye
blurb: The London Eye, originally the Millennium Wheel, is a cantilevered observation wheel on the South Bank of the River Thames in London. Its 120 m steel rim hangs on 64 tensioned cables from a central hub, and its 32 passenger capsules turn on a 22 m spindle held by a leaning A-frame.

sourceUrls.label: New Civil Engineer: Eye’s wide open in time for Millennium
New Civil Engineer: A view to a thrill
New Civil Engineer: Turning to analysis
Mechanical Engineering: Building the world’s biggest wheel

systems.name: Wheel rim
systems.description: The 120 m steel rim, built in sections that were floated up the Thames on barges and assembled lying flat on piled platforms in the river before the wheel was raised.

systems.name: Tension cables
systems.description: Sixty-four tensioned steel cables carry the rim like the spokes of a huge bicycle wheel, each prestressed to 75 tonnes; sixteen rotation cables keep the rim and hub turning together.

systems.name: Hub and spindle
systems.description: The wheel and hub turn on bearings around a fixed 22 m spindle, which cantilevers out over the Thames from the A-frame.

systems.name: Passenger capsules
systems.description: Thirty-two sealed, air-conditioned ovoidal capsules, each weighing 10 tonnes and holding up to 25 people, numbered 1 to 33 with 13 skipped.

systems.name: A-frame support
systems.description: Two tapered legs, each over 58 m long and 20 m apart at the base, leaning toward the river at 65 degrees and held by cable backstays.

systems.name: Drive and restraint towers
systems.description: Short towers founded in the river bed carry the rim-bearing drive units, which turn the wheel by friction against the rim.

systems.name: Boarding platform
systems.description: The deck, ticket hall, canopy and gangways where passengers walk on and off the moving capsules; the wheel does not usually stop for boarding.

systems.name: LED lighting
systems.description: LED lighting from Color Kinetics, installed in December 2006, for digital control of the rim colors.

systems.name: Foundations
systems.description: The plinths, foundation raft and tension anchor blocks that hold the A-frame and its backstays.

They hang on the external circumference of the wheel and are rotated by electric motors so the floor stays level. Exact size and shape are schematic.
